課.meaning: At the jungle school, the gorilla teacher gives every <part>speech</part> with his mouth full of <part>fruit</part>, spraying mango over the front row. The monkeys write it all down on banana leaves and staple them into a book. Today they finish another juicy <kanji>chapter</kanji>.
課.on: The class pet, a fat <sound>ca</sound>rp in a bucket, gets all the mango peel.

府.meaning: A tiny town keeps adding things to its only garden <part>shed</part>: they <part>attach</part> a post office, then a library, then a bus stop, each nailed to the side. Soon the shed has its own mayor, flag and bin collection. It's become an official <kanji>borough</kanji>.
府.on: The mayor runs it all from a <sound>fu</sound>ton in the corner.

県.meaning: A nosy giant lies across the countryside with one <part>eye</part> open, keeping watch over the <part>little</part> farms between his fingers. Each farmer pays him a turnip a year to keep the foxes away. Everything he can see from there counts as one <kanji>prefecture</kanji>.
県.on: His pet wolf sleeps in a <sound>ken</sound>nel the size of a barn.
県.kun: At supper time he hangs a <sound>ca</sound>rp from a hook above the kennel door.

幕.meaning: A theatre can't afford velvet, so the cleaner sews every beach <part>towel</part> in the building into one huge sheet, printed with a palm-tree <part>sunset</part>. When the play ends, it drops with a damp thump and a whiff of sun cream. That's the theatre's new <kanji>curtain</kanji>.
幕.on: Backstage it drips <sound>muc</sound>k from the beach all over the actors' shoes.
幕.kun: On <sound>to</sound>p of the rail, a stagehand cooks a <sound>ba</sound>rbecue, and smoke drifts through the <sound>ree</sound>ds painted along its hem.

砲.meaning: A tidy giant decides to <part>pack up</part> his rock collection and post it to his cousin, so he stuffs every <part>stone</part> into a long iron tube and lights the end. Boom: the parcel flies over three hills. He's invented express mail, by <kanji>cannon</kanji>.
砲.on: The cousin puts out the smoking rocks with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se.

就.meaning: In the busy <part>capital</part>, a man with a <part>broken crutch</part> limps into the king's office with a long letter. 'This is about the potholes,' he says, waving it. The king sighs and reads every page of a letter <kanji>concerning</kanji> his roads.
就.on: As proof, the man also hands over his worn-out <sound>shoe</sound>.
就.kun: The king sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' into the letter, then takes his seat at the desk to deal with it.

幼.meaning: A baby in a high chair grips a tiny <part>twist</part> of pretzel and, with every scrap of <part>muscle</part>, bends the whole chair in half. The nurses stare. If he can do that already, imagine him at five. He's still in his <kanji>infancy</kanji>.
幼.on: His favourite toy is a <sound>yo</sound>-yo that he swings like a wrecking ball.
幼.kun: At lunch he waves a toy <sound>o</sound>ctopus, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a scrap of <sound>na</sound>an, far too little to eat any of them.

敵.meaning: Every night a moth flutters toward the <part>hanging lantern</part> on the porch, and every night grandpa waves it away with a paper <part>fan</part>. Flap, flap, swat, miss. They've fought for forty summers, and each respects the other: a true <kanji>enemy</kanji>.
敵.on: One night the moth sends him a <sound>tex</sound>t message: 'See you tomorrow.'
敵.kun: Grandpa stocks up for the next fight: a <sound>ca</sound>rp bone, a <sound>ta</sound>co crumb and a <sound>ki</sound>wi skin to throw.
